intro: one person in chiang mai · solo by default, a team when the work needs one
i build worlds that remember themselves, so they keep running when nobody is watching.

rows.name: living memory
rows.desc: a shared world your agents step into. tell one agent something today, ask a different one about it tomorrow.

rows.name: wink grooming
rows.desc: a cat hotel my partner and i designed, paid for and built from nothing. she runs it remotely for months at a time. its own agent answers guests now.

rows.name: homelog
rows.desc: access and timeline for a real building, built to outlive whoever is on shift.

rows.name: squish
rows.desc: agents read video instead of transcripts.

notes.label: the through-line
notes.text: all of them are the same problem: a place that has to work when its owner is not there.

notes.label: learned the hard way
notes.text: wink's customers were never on the website — they were on google maps the whole time. the site had been dark for years and was not worth reviving until now.

notes.label: this month
notes.text: two hackathons · teaching a shop to talk to other people's agents

notes.label: open for
notes.text: local work in chiang mai. i'm easy to find, and i answer email.
